title: How much of the whole chikki is each of the eight pieces?
description: Eight chikki pieces of different shapes are each named as a fraction of the whole chikki. The squares in each piece are counted, then the number of copies that fill the whole is found and checked.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the squares in a piece, then ask how many such pieces fill the whole. Watch for students who count every square a triangle touches instead of the half it covers.

source: The figures below show different fractional units of a whole chikki. How much of a whole chikki is each piece?
video_script.why: The child names any piece of the chikki, whatever its shape, by counting the squares it covers and how many such pieces fill the whole.
video_script.substitution: Measure every piece in small squares; a triangle cut corner to corner covers half of its rectangle.
video_script.anchor: Eight chikki pieces of different shapes shown beside one whole chikki of 24 small squares, 6 across and 4 down
video_script.payoff_line: Each piece is named by how many copies of it fill the chikki

final_answer.spoken: one twelfth, one fourth, one eighth, one sixth, one eighth, one sixth, one twenty fourth, one twenty fourth

video_script.fraction_reading: one twelfth, one fourth, one eighth, one sixth, one twenty fourth
never_show: any of the eight fractions before the answer beat
maths_rules: whole chikki: 6 across, 4 down, 6 x 4 = 24 small squares
a triangle cut corner to corner from a block covers half of the block's squares
rectangle 1 across, 2 down: 2 squares; 24 / 2 = 12 copies, so 1/12
big triangle, half of a 3 by 4 block: 12 / 2 = 6 squares; 24 / 6 = 4 copies, so 1/4
small triangle, half of a 3 by 2 block: 6 / 2 = 3 squares; 24 / 3 = 8 copies, so 1/8
thin strip 1 across, 4 down: 4 squares; 24 / 4 = 6 copies, so 1/6
L shape of 3 squares: 24 / 3 = 8 copies, so 1/8
long triangle, half of a 2 by 4 block: 8 / 2 = 4 squares; 24 / 4 = 6 copies, so 1/6
tiny triangle, half of a 1 by 2 block: 2 / 2 = 1 square; so 1/24
check: squares in a piece x copies = 24 for every piece
video_script.design: One idea: count the squares in a piece, then count how many copies fill the whole. Same method as the strip question. The whole chikki and the eight pieces stay on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step one, count the squares in each piece. A triangle cut corner to corner covers half of its block.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The rectangle covers two squares, the big triangle six, and the small triangle three.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The thin strip covers four squares, and the L shape covers three squares.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The long triangle covers four squares, and the single square covers one. The tiny triangle also covers one square.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: copies that fill 24 squares: rectangle 24 / 2 = 12, big triangle 24 / 6 = 4, small triangle 24 / 3 = 8, thin strip 24 / 4 = 6, L shape 8, long triangle 6, single square 24, tiny triangle 24

marks.second: copies of the thin strip, the L shape and the long triangle fill the chikki and are counted
marks.third: copies of the single square and the tiny triangle fill the chikki and are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='ask'/>Step two, ask how many copies of a piece fill the whole chikki.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Divide twenty four by the squares in the piece, the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The rectangle needs twelve copies, the big triangle four, and the small triangle eight.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The thin strip needs six copies, the L shape eight, and the long triangle six.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The single square and the tiny triangle each need twenty four copies.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: check, squares in a piece x copies = 24 for every piece: 2 x 12, 6 x 4, 3 x 8, 4 x 6, 3 x 8, 4 x 6, 1 x 24, 1 x 24

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, check every piece. The squares in a piece times its copies must make twenty four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two times twelve is twenty four, and six times four is twenty four. Every other piece also passes.

beats.on_screen: Answer: rectangle 1/12, big triangle 1/4, small triangle 1/8, thin strip 1/6, L shape 1/8, long triangle 1/6, single square 1/24, tiny triangle 1/24

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each piece is named by how many copies of it fill the chikki.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The rectangle is one twelfth, the big triangle is one fourth, and the small triangle is one eighth.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The thin strip is one sixth and the L shape is one eighth. The long triangle is one sixth.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The single square and the tiny triangle are each one twenty fourth of the chikki.
